items.stem: Why is a quality-of-earnings analysis central to financial due diligence?

options.text: It distinguishes sustainable, normalised earnings from one-off or non-recurring items
options.rationale: Correct: QoE separates recurring earning power from noise.

options.text: It re-audits the statutory accounts for an opinion
options.rationale: DD is not a statutory audit.

options.text: It sets the legal structure of the deal
options.rationale: Structure is a legal, not a QoE, matter.

options.text: It guarantees the forecast will be achieved
options.rationale: QoE assesses history; it does not guarantee forecasts.

items.explanation: Correct: QoE separates sustainable, normalised earnings from one-off items.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO items are typically treated as debt-like when calculating net debt? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: a committed outflow behaves like debt.
These sit in working capital, not net debt.
Inventory is a working-capital item, not debt-like.

items.explanation: Correct: declared-unpaid dividends and overdue tax are committed outflows treated as debt-like.

items.stem: A DD finding shows working capital was unusually low at the measurement date due to delayed supplier payments. What is the right response?

options.text: Reflect it in a normalised working-capital peg so the buyer is not short-changed
options.rationale: Correct: normalising the peg prevents a value transfer from the buyer.

options.text: Ignore it because it is only timing
options.rationale: Timing distortions directly affect value at completion.

options.text: Automatically reduce the headline price by the same amount
options.rationale: The mechanism is the peg, not an automatic price cut.
A balance-sheet timing item is not earnings.

items.explanation: Correct: a normalised working-capital peg handles the timing distortion fairly.
